bullets.title: June NFP miss at +57k signals softening labor market; Fed on hold, July hike off table
bullets.body: June nonfarm payrolls came in at +57k vs. consensus of ~113-115k, with prior months revised down a cumulative -74k, bringing the 3-month average to ~111k. The unemployment rate fell to 4.19-4.2% but was entirely driven by an anomalous 720k collapse in labor force participation (98th percentile move), concentrated in 25-34 year-olds; the employment/population ratio fell sharply, suggesting the labor market actually eased. Consensus across Morgan Stanley, PSC Macro, and Wolfe is that the data keeps the Fed on hold through 2026—no July hike—while not materially changing eventual hiking odds given ~4.5% aggregate wage growth and sticky core inflation.

bullets.title: Core inflation sticky near 3% even as oil decline sets up headline relief in 2H26
bullets.body: JPMorgan's global inflation monitor notes June's sharp oil price decline should push headline CPI below ~2% in 2H26 if Brent holds current levels, effectively removing a dual shock to growth and inflation. However, core inflation remains stuck near 3%, driven by firm services price pressures that central banks must still contend with. The 22V base case keeps core PCE near 0.21% MoM, making a September rate hike unlikely.

bullets.title: META's cloud compute monetization sparks AI capex debate; semis sold off sharply
bullets.body: META's announcement that it would lease excess AI compute capacity at ~65% utilization triggered a violent repricing: SOX -9%, momentum basket -10% (worst day since 2020), NBIS and CRWV down 17% and 14% respectively. The debate splits between bears (signals AI overbuild, demand hasn't absorbed $1.1T in compute commitments) and bulls (META boosting ROIC and FCF to fund continued capex; AI demand still running ~4x available supply). Citi maintains Buy on META ($850 PT), framing compute monetization as FCF-accretive while funding Prometheus/Hyperion builds; Jefferies also Buy ($825 PT, 46% upside).

bullets.title: JPM revises AI server/networking TAMs higher +9-20%; CRDO holds 82% AEC chip share
bullets.body: Despite the selloff, JPMorgan revised hardware and networking TAMs upward: AI Servers +9/+12/+20% for '26/'27/'28, DC Ethernet Switch +2/+12/+7%, DCI +15/+22/+28%, with AI servers growing at +37% CAGR through 2030. DELL is gaining server share (21% in 1Q26 vs. 10% YoY), ANET leads DC Ethernet at 22%, and CRDO holds ~82% AEC chip share. Options traders are shifting regime: selling 6-month upside vol and buying 2-month downside vol across semi equipment, memory, and photonics.

bullets.title: Memory 'chipflation' emerges as hidden cost shock; UBS raises ASML EPS 9-14% on memory demand
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flags 'chipflation'—memory chip prices rising sharply on AI demand—marking the end of the falling-cost era and posing a structural cost headwind to AI infrastructure builds. UBS raised ASML 2027/28 EPS another 9%/14% (now 22%/33% above consensus), driven by a forecast for memory revenues to grow +50% in 2027.

bullets.title: Citi lifts S&P 500 year-end target to 8,100; pre-market futures +0.19% post-NFP
bullets.body: Citi raised its S&P 500 year-end target to 8,100 based on $350/$400 EPS for 2026/2027. Pre-market S&P futures were +14.5 points (+0.19%) to 7,558 after the NFP print, with 10-year yields +1bp to 4.47% and WTI crude -1.36% to $67.65. Citi's Economics team had forecast an even more dovish 25k payroll print.

bullets.title: European hedge fund positioning: Tech overweight highest since Feb 2018; Financials at lowest since Jun 2020
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs June prime services data shows European fundamental L/S managers added 2.3pts to their tech overweight to +7.7%, the highest since February 2018, while cutting Financials by 3.8pts to -6.8%, the lowest since June 2020. European equities were the most net-sold regional allocation, driven by macro product short selling. Global Fundamental L/S up +17.4% YTD vs. MSCI World +9.7%.

bullets.title: Russell 2000 outperformance expected to moderate in 2H26 as AI tailwind fades post-reconstitution
bullets.body: Goldman's Ben Snider notes the Russell 2000 gained 23% YTD and 41% over 12 months, outperforming the S&P 500 by 12pp YTD, with AI infrastructure stocks driving ~40% of returns—but their index weight was cut from 15% to 7% post-reconstitution. Consensus still calls for Russell 2000 EPS growth of 48% vs. 24% for S&P 500 in 2026, but elevated dispersion favors stock-picking over index exposure. Biotech M&A was also a tailwind, with $236B announced in 1H26, up 90% YoY.

bullets.title: Infrastructure software +18.5% YTD vs. application software -26.5%; large-cap software down 33.5%
bullets.body: KeyBanc data shows a stark 45-percentage-point YTD gap between infrastructure-exposed software (MSFT, ORCL, NET) and application software. Large-cap software names (MSFT, ORCL, CRM, NOW, SAP, ADBE) are down 33.5% equal-weighted YTD with no defensive qualities apparent in the 2026 downturn. Performance dispersion is extreme: top quintile +49% vs. bottom quintile -55.8% YTD.

bullets.title: OpenAI proposing 5% US government equity stake; SpaceX developing AI handset threatening telcos
bullets.body: Citi flags two policy/tech-structure headlines: OpenAI is proposing to hand a 5% stake to the US government as part of a Trump administration deal, with other AI labs potentially following. Separately, SpaceX is developing an AI handset running a proprietary OS with xAI tech and Snapdragon chipset, representing a potential threat to TMUS/VZ/T in the connectivity space.

bullets.title: NY legislature considering 1-year data center permit moratorium; fuel cells emerging as emissions solution
bullets.body: The NY Responsible Data Center Development Act would impose a 1-year pause on data center permits, pending governor approval. Meanwhile, Morgan Stanley notes 74 planned US behind-the-meter gas power projects for data centers could generate 143 GW and 662M tons annual GHG, making fuel cells an emerging regulatory solution to local air emission concerns.

bullets.title: BoE mixed signals: Bailey dovish despite above-3% inflation; Mann flags case for tightening
bullets.body: JPMorgan's UK economics note shows Governor Bailey reiterating a dovish bias—arguing the BoE would have cut twice absent the Iran conflict—while MPC member Catherine Mann signals that tightening could have been warranted in June given elevated inflation expectations. Core UK inflation is expected to rise to 2.8% YoY in autumn, with upside surprises set to pressure the MPC. Quoted mortgage rates are likely to fall sharply in Q3 as markets price out hikes.

bullets.title: Ad checks: budgets finishing 2Q better than expected; AMZN DSP and APP gaining share vs. TTD, SNAP, PINS
bullets.body: UBS ad channel checks show Q2 finishing better than feared, with performance advertising gaining share over brand platforms. AMZN DSP and AppLovin are the standout winners; TTD, SNAP, and PINS remain under pressure from brand-spend weakness. Roth Capital separately flags advertiser consideration of shifting budgets toward ChatGPT ads, with tier-2 platforms (TikTok, Reddit, Pinterest) also gaining traction.

bullets.title: DISH files Chapter 11; ~$5B debt exits HY indices July 31; HY default rate rises to 1.21%
bullets.body: DISH DBS and wireless subsidiaries filed Chapter 11 on June 30, 2026. The ~$5B of indexed debt (25bps weight in GCI HY USD) will be removed at July month-end rebalance, pushing the HY USD default rate from 0.95% to 1.21%, with total 2026 HY defaults now at $22.675B.

bullets.title: TSLA Q2 deliveries 480k, +25% YoY, beating 397k consensus; energy storage 13.5 GWh
bullets.body: Tesla Q2 deliveries came in at 480k (+25% YoY) versus consensus of 397k, a meaningful beat. Energy storage of 13.5 GWh (+34% YoY) was a slight miss vs. the 13.9 GWh consensus. Saudi crude shipments separately recovering toward 2025 levels (6.3 mmbbl/d, up from 4.45 in June), supporting a lower oil price base case.

bullets.title: Fed shifting from forward guidance to reaction-function communication; Warsh reaffirms price stability mandate
bullets.body: Chair Warsh reaffirmed the Fed's commitment to price stability while noting AI-driven productivity could improve the supply side. 22V notes the Fed is actively moving away from forward guidance toward communicating its reaction function, with inflation and labor data the sole determinants of the policy path. A September rate hike remains unlikely under the base case.

bullets.title: GOOGL's $4.7B EU antitrust fine upheld by top court; also ordered to pay Klarna $1.5B
bullets.body: The EU's highest court upheld Google's record €4.13B ($4.7B) antitrust fine over Android anti-competitive practices. Google was separately ordered to pay Klarna $1.5B in antitrust damages. Meta also lost a bid to dismiss state claims alleging Facebook and Instagram addict children.

bullets.title: SUPER MICRO raided in Taiwan chip-smuggling probe; SMCI stock under pressure
bullets.body: Taiwan authorities expanded a chip-smuggling investigation to include Super Micro Computer, conducting a raid. The development adds regulatory and reputational risk to SMCI at a time when the stock is already under scrutiny.

bullets.title: Piper Sandler sees 2H26 outperformance in housing-adjacent retail on falling yields and valuation expansion
bullets.body: Piper Sandler identifies HD, W, FND, and SGI as top picks for 2H26, citing valuation expansion, improving fundamentals, expected further declines in the 10-year yield, and constructive technical setups. Consumer spending pickup is anticipated as a secondary catalyst.

bullets.title: Goldman Communacopia Tech Conference (Sept 8-11, SF): 100+ companies; CRWD, INTC, TWLO added
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference is set for September 8-11 at the Palace Hotel in San Francisco, with investor meeting requests due by July 21. New additions include CrowdStrike (CRWD), Intel (INTC), and Twilio (TWLO), with Databricks hosting 1x1s despite remaining private.
